lead: A directional coupler is a four-port microwave component that samples a small, known fraction of the wave travelling from port 1 to port 2 and sends it to a coupled port 3. The fourth port, port 4, should receive almost nothing; how little it receives is set by the isolation I, which equals the coupling plus the directivity, I = C + D. A hybrid ring is a four-port ring that splits power equally between two outputs and fixes a 180° phase relation, so it can add or subtract two signals. Both are built from waveguides, microstrip or stripline and are used in power monitoring, balanced mixers, reflectometers and antenna feeds.
prereq: You need S-parameters from 4.1 and tee junctions from 4.2.

blocks.text: Number the ports in the usual way: port 1 is the input, port 2 is the through port, port 3 is the coupled port and port 4 is the isolated port. With all ports matched, S₃₁ is the outgoing wave at port 3 divided by the wave incident at port 1. Its magnitude is small, so the coupling is written as a positive number of decibels.
C = −20 log₁₀ |S₃₁| dB,   I = −20 log₁₀ |S₄₁| dB,   D = I − C = −20 log₁₀ (|S₄₁|/|S₃₁|) dB
blocks.where: S₃₁ and S₄₁ are voltage-wave ratios from the scattering matrix; C is coupling in dB; I is isolation in dB; D is directivity in dB.

blocks.text: A 10 dB coupler has |S₃₁| = 0.316, so 10% of the input power reaches port 3. A 20 dB coupler sends 1%. The through port gets most of the remaining power. The isolated port is not perfect: leakage through it is set by I. Directivity compares the wanted coupled wave with that leakage, so a large D means a clean coupler. Practical waveguide couplers give D of about 20 dB to 40 dB. The coupled wave also has a phase relative to the input; C gives only magnitude. The phase is set by the coupler design and must be checked separately. For a matched, reciprocal coupler the S-matrix is four by four: the diagonal terms are zero in the ideal case, S₂₁ is the through term, S₃₁ is the coupled term and S₄₁ is the isolated term.

sections.h3: Two-hole coupler and the hybrid ring

blocks.text: A two-hole directional coupler uses two small holes, spaced a quarter of a guide wavelength λg apart, in the wall between two waveguides. Power leaks through both holes. In the forward direction the two leaked waves travel equal extra paths and add. In the reverse direction they differ by λg/2 and cancel. This is why a two-hole coupler has directivity: it favours one direction. The full field theory of the holes is not needed for exams; remember the quarter-wave spacing and the add/cancel picture.

A hybrid ring, also called a rat-race, is a closed ring of circumference 3λg/2 with four ports. Number them in order around the ring as 1, 2, 3, 4. Three arcs are λg/4 (between 1-2, 2-3 and 3-4) and one arc is 3λg/4 (between 4 and 1). The 3λg/4 arm is λg/4 longer than the other three, so it adds 180° relative to them. Port 1 is the sum port and port 3 is the difference port. Feed the sum port (port 1): ports 2 and 4 get equal power in phase, and port 3 is isolated. Feed the difference port (port 3): ports 2 and 4 get equal power with 180° between them, and port 1 is isolated. This sum-and-difference action is used in balanced mixers, push-pull amplifiers and monopulse antenna comparators. A branch-line hybrid is the 90° relative: it uses λg/4 arms and gives a 90° phase difference between outputs. A magic tee from 4.2 is another 180° hybrid, but in waveguide form.

figure.caption: Port 1 feeds the coupler; port 2 is the through path, port 3 takes the 10 dB coupled sample, and port 4 takes leakage 30 dB below input.

spec.aria: Four-port directional coupler: input at port 1 gives a through wave at port 2, a 10 dB coupled wave at port 3 and a 30 dB isolated wave at port 4.

examples.question: A directional coupler is fed with 20 dBm at port 1. Its coupling is 10 dB and its directivity is 20 dB. The other ports are matched. Find the power at the coupled port and at the isolated port, in dBm and mW.
steps: Coupling gives P₃ = P₁ − C = 20 dBm − 10 dB = 10 dBm.
Convert the coupled power: P₃ = 10^(10/10) mW = 10 mW.
Isolation is I = C + D = 10 dB + 20 dB = 30 dB.
The isolated-port power is P₄ = P₁ − I = 20 dBm − 30 dB = −10 dBm.
Convert the isolated power: P₄ = 10^(−10/10) mW = 0.1 mW.
examples.answer: The coupled port delivers 10 dBm (10 mW), and the isolated port delivers −10 dBm (0.1 mW).
examples.check:
P1_dBm = 20.0
C_dB = 10.0
D_dB = 20.0
P3_dBm = P1_dBm - C_dB
I_dB = C_dB + D_dB
P4_dBm = P1_dBm - I_dB
P3_mW = 10 ** (P3_dBm / 10)
P4_mW = 10 ** (P4_dBm / 10)
print(P3_dBm)
print(P3_mW)
print(I_dB)
print(P4_dBm)
print(P4_mW)

traps: Coupling is not directivity. Coupling compares port 3 with port 1; directivity compares port 4 leakage with port 3.
Use 10 log for power ratios and 20 log only for voltage-wave ratios such as |S|. Mixing them shifts every answer by a factor of 2.
The isolated-port level uses I = C + D, not D alone. Subtracting D from the input is a common error.
Do not assume port 4 is zero. Real isolation is finite; a 20 dB directivity coupler still leaks.
C and I give magnitudes only. The coupled port has a designed phase; skip it and a phase question loses marks.

quiz.q: Define coupling and isolation of a four-port directional coupler in dB.
Why does a large directivity matter in a reflectometer?
quiz.a: It keeps backward leakage at port 4 from adding to the coupled sample, so the measured reflection is not masked by directivity error.

quiz.q: A 20 dB coupler with 25 dB directivity is fed with 30 dBm. Find the coupled and isolated powers.
Explain the quarter-wave hole spacing in a two-hole directional coupler.
quiz.a: Forward leaked waves from the two holes add; reverse leaked waves differ by λg/2 and cancel, giving directivity.

quiz.q: State the circumference and port spacing of a rat-race hybrid ring.
quiz.a: Circumference 3λg/2; three spacings of λg/4 and one spacing of 3λg/4.

quiz.q: Give one difference between a rat-race hybrid and a branch-line hybrid.
quiz.a: A rat-race gives 180° phase relation and has one 3λg/4 arm; a branch-line hybrid gives 90° and uses λg/4 arms.

quiz.q: A rat-race is fed at its sum port (port 1). What are the relative phases at the two output ports, and which port is isolated?
quiz.a: Ports 2 and 4 are equal in phase; port 3 (the difference port) is isolated.

quiz.q: Why is the isolated port of a real coupler not exactly zero?
quiz.a: Directivity is finite, and reflections plus construction imperfections produce small leakage at the isolated port.

beyond: Not for the exam. Modern couplers are printed on PCB, LTCC and MMIC substrates; coupled-line and Lange couplers reach tight coupling in a small area. Rat-race hybrids appear in balanced amplifiers, image-reject mixers and monopulse comparator networks. Search next for coupled-line directional coupler, Lange coupler, rat-race hybrid S-parameters and six-port reflectometer.
